press.quote: Hoffmann proves that photography can still surprise — these images are genuinely new.
press.author: Carmen Okafor

aboutLead: I'm a photographer and installation artist based in Berlin. My work investigates attention — what we see when we truly stop to look, and what slips past us in the ordinary flow of a day.
aboutBody: Born in Munich in 1989, I studied Fine Art at the Hochschule für Bildende Künste in Hamburg and Photography at the Royal College of Art in London, where I received my MA in 2015. I have lived and worked in Berlin since 2016.

My photographic practice is built on sustained, slow observation. I often return to a location dozens of times before making an image. The final photographs are typically long exposures — anywhere from four minutes to half an hour — made with available light only. The resulting images hover between documentation and abstraction, between the familiar and the strange.

My installation work begins from photography but expands into physical space, often incorporating found objects and architectural intervention. Both practices share a preoccupation with the overlooked: the things in our peripheral vision that accumulate into the texture of lived experience.
I have exhibited internationally and my work is held in several private collections in Germany and Switzerland. I am represented in Europe by Galerie Nord Tiergarten, Berlin.
